mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.0% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a financial crisis with inverted yield curve.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth falls below -2% and remains below for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP contraction is accompanied by strong monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 8.0% and remains above for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation offsetting labor weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by strong consumer demand proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during deflationary periods.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to rapid earnings downgrades.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by more than 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5% while payrolls (PAYEMS) grow above their 12-month average, it signals a tight labor market with upward wage pressure, which raises input costs and compresses margins, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in late-cycle conditions.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% AND PAYEMS > 12-month average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered late-cycle months, or the mechanism fails during periods of falling inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Real Savings Rate (RSAFS) above its 5-year average for three consecutive months signals increased precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 65% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong monetary stimulus.
